title: Root nonce is a strictly increasing odometer
statement: SmartAccount.root_nonce increases by exactly 1 on every successful root instruction and never decreases, so no assertion is consumable twice.
spec_ref: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-18-warden-wallet-design.md#4 (root nonce = an odometer, not a set)
notes: Monotonicity is item (3) on the L6 Certora proof order; until then this is test-covered only. Storage is O(1): there is no consumed-nonce set to grow.

title: Strict n+1 equality, not a window
statement: A transcript whose root_nonce is not exactly equal to the stored value is rejected; there is no acceptance window and no replay bitmap.
notes: Do not replace with a set- or window-based scheme; strict n+1 is what makes a captured assertion dead the instant any other root instruction lands.

title: Slot-based root freshness
statement: A root ceremony is accepted only while signed_slot <= Clock::slot < signed_slot + MAX_ROOT_SLOT_AGE (150): a future slot is rejected outright and an age of exactly 150 slots is rejected.
notes: Landed by Task 0 (F) in 26a8c1e. Both halves of the inequality are covered by named boundary tests: age 0 and 149 accepted, 150 rejected, future-by-one rejected, u64::MAX treated as future rather than overflowing. `valid_expiry_does_not_rescue_a_stale_slot` and its mirror prove the two clocks are independent bounds, not alternatives.

title: Wall-clock expiry is the secondary bound
statement: expiry_ts must satisfy now <= expiry_ts <= now + 600s; an expired transcript and one expiring beyond the 600s horizon are both rejected, and the 600s boundary itself is accepted.
notes: Clock::unix_timestamp is a stake-weighted estimate; once WRD-NONCE-03 lands this stays only as the secondary bound and as the sole bound on 1C's deferred queue/execute_pending path.

title: Cap dominance
statement: Every accepted spend satisfies amount <= min(per_tx, per_day - spent_today, per_30d - sum(ring)), and for a session additionally lifetime_spent + amount <= lifetime_cap.
notes: Item (2) on the L6 Certora proof order. Not yet mutation-tested: cargo-mutants is unpiloted on this workspace (spec 17 L4), and buckets.rs is the designated pilot module.

title: Bucket accounting is exact and the ring self-cleans
statement: spent_today equals the sum of the day's debits, sum(ring) <= per_30d, and no ring slot survives a rollover that should have zeroed it.
notes: Item (1) on the L6 Certora proof order. Codex's own reimplementation of this ring in the 1A pilot wrote the closed day to ring[kept-1] instead of ring[RING_DAYS-1], permanently understating 30-day spend; the differential test is what caught it, so keep the reference model.

title: No cap means zero, never unlimited
statement: A mint with no cap entry (and a zeroed cap entry) permits outflow of exactly 0; the missing-cap branch rejects rather than skipping the check.
notes: find_cap must never match the all-zero default Pubkey, or an unconfigured slot silently becomes a cap for mint 11111...; that is asserted separately.

title: An expired or revoked session is exhausted, not absent
statement: A session past expiry_ts, with a stale generation_at_grant, revoked, or belonging to another account is treated as having zero remaining allowance on every axis, never as an account with no cap configured.
notes: This is the exact shape of LazorKit ACC-C2 (an authorisation branch that skipped a check instead of failing it) and it is the difference between a fail-closed and a fail-open wallet. Every new 1B comparison must be written the same way.

title: Root direct `transfer` is bounded like a session
statement: The root `transfer` path enforces outflow[mint] <= large_threshold[mint] per transaction AND debits the same account-wide day and rolling-30-day buckets that sessions debit.
notes: SCOPED TO `transfer` DELIBERATELY. The spec states the same rule for the root `execute` and `swap` paths, but no such path exists yet and no test covers it -- that is WRD-CAP-09, seeded separately at `unimplemented`. Rolling the two into one row would have let a 1A test stand as evidence for a 1B surface.

title: Debit is atomic
statement: A debit that is going to be rejected leaves every bucket field byte-identical to its pre-call value, including when the rejection happens after a day-boundary rollover or an arithmetic overflow guard fires.
notes: The rollover is the dangerous half: it mutates state before the cap comparison, so a non-atomic implementation would leak a free day of allowance on every rejected spend.

title: Day and 30-day windows are account-wide, not per session
statement: Every session and the root debit the same SmartAccount.buckets, so N sessions do not get N day caps; and a grant that sets a non-zero per-session per_day/per_30d is rejected rather than stored.
notes: 1B keeps rejecting per-session day caps at grant. Per-session day buckets are 1C and ride on the single DayBuckets PDA (spec 5.2 rule 4c).

title: Session lifetime cap is exact and survives a regrant
statement: lifetime_spent + amount <= lifetime_cap on every session spend, a regrant merges by mint while preserving spent, and a regrant that would set a lifetime cap below what has already been spent is rejected.
notes: prior_authority_hash is what makes the merge bind the authority it produces rather than only the fields it names; that is the LZR-ACC-H1 shape (accounts/fields omitted from the signed payload).

title: Root `execute` and `swap` are bounded like a session
statement: The root `execute` and `swap` paths enforce outflow[mint] <= large_threshold[mint] per transaction AND debit the same account-wide day and rolling-30-day buckets. (Phase 1B scope only: the `execute_pending` conjunct of the original statement moved to WRD-CAP-10 when WRDF-0108 showed this row was promoted while certifying an unbuilt path.)
notes: Split out of WRD-CAP-05 so a 1A `transfer` test can never stand as evidence for a 1B surface. The one-line consequence this row protects: a root attacker without guardians extracts at most the account-wide day bucket per day and the 30-day cap per month, across EVERY root path -- which is false the moment one root path skips the buckets. B4 (2026-08-23): previously NO test asserted the bucket debit actually happened on either 1B surface, and both over-threshold negatives were session-path (not root). Now the root execute and root swap happy paths assert day + rolling-30-day ring debits on the right bucket slot with the other slot untouched, and both surfaces have a root over-threshold negative. Caveat: on swap, swap_policy sets caps.per_tx == large_threshold.per_tx, so the pre-CPI bucket probe refuses max_in before the large_threshold rung is reached; the execute counterpart does hit large_threshold directly. Mint-absent-from-large_threshold is covered (absent means not allowed, never unlimited). WRDF-0108 (2026-08-23, Codex round 390ff37d26a3): this row was promoted to test-covered on 5 tests covering root execute + root swap ONLY, while its statement also promised that `execute_pending` debits the buckets — an unbuilt Phase 1C path. That is the SAME defect the same pass correctly avoided on WRD-FRZ-03, so the promotion was inconsistent, not merely optimistic. Root cause: coverage was checked against a TRUNCATED reading of the statement; the trailing conjunct was never read. Resolved by splitting rather than reverting: the 1B execute/swap evidence is real and stays here; the execute_pending conjunct is now WRD-CAP-10 and remains unimplemented.

title: Amounts above the per-transaction threshold require execute_pending, which also debits the buckets
statement: An outflow larger than large_threshold[mint] must come from `execute_pending`, whose execution also debits the account-wide day and rolling-30-day buckets, so the queued path cannot be used to bypass the windowed budgets.
notes: Split out of WRD-CAP-09 on WRDF-0108 (2026-08-23). `execute_pending` does not exist in the program (grep: only docs/ mention it), so NO evidence can satisfy this row until Phase 1C. Promotion requires a real execute_pending bucket-debit test, plus an over-threshold amount actually routed through it. Sibling of WRD-FRZ-03, which is blocked on the same unbuilt handler.

title: ops_mask is bounded by the ceiling AND by the assigned bits
statement: A grant is rejected unless ops_mask is a subset of policy.session_ops_ceiling AND a subset of the bits this program version has actually assigned; an unassigned bit is refused rather than stored, and an operation whose bit is unset is rejected at use.
notes: The unassigned-bit refusal is the load-bearing half and is easy to omit: an unassigned bit stored today silently becomes real authority the day a later version assigns it. Refusing at grant, not at use, is what makes that impossible.

title: Session caps may not exceed the policy ceiling
statement: Every per-mint cap in a grant is <= policy.session_ceiling for that mint, a mint with no session ceiling cannot be granted at all, and the ceiling itself cannot be set above the account cap at creation.
notes: The boundary-accepted test matters as much as the rejections: an off-by-one that rejected a grant exactly AT the ceiling would be a silent usability bug nobody reports, and it is the same code path that an off-by-one in the other direction breaks security.

title: Session expiry is bounded and must be in the future
statement: A grant's expiry_ts must be strictly in the future and no later than now + policy.max_session_life; the max_session_life boundary itself is accepted, and a policy setting max_session_life above 30 days is refused at creation.
notes: Expiry is one of the three axes on which an expired session must read as EXHAUSTED rather than ABSENT (WRD-CAP-04); this row covers the grant-time bound, WRD-CAP-04 covers the use-time behaviour.

title: generation_at_grant is refreshed at grant and matched at use
statement: A grant records the account's current generation, a regrant refreshes it, and a session whose generation_at_grant does not equal the account's current generation cannot act.
notes: Same evidence caveat as WRD-ROOT-08: generation is advanced by a helper, not by a real execute_recovery (WRD-ROOT-11). This proves the match, not the bump.

title: A regrant binds the authority it produces, not only the fields it names
statement: A merging grant carries prior_authority_hash -- the hash of the retained identity, every cap slot and every lifetime cap it is allowed to merge into -- a mismatch is refused, a fresh grant must carry the zero sentinel, and a regrant must not carry it.
notes: This is the LZR-ACC-H1 lesson generalised: it is not enough for the signed payload to name the fields it changes; it must bind the state it merges into, or a signature over a partial view authorises an authority the signer never saw.

title: Only the root or the session itself may revoke it
statement: revoke_session succeeds for a root ceremony over that exact session and for the session key signing for itself, and fails for a stranger, for a root ceremony naming a different session account, and for a substituted rent-refund destination.
notes: The substituted-refund case is the rent-theft shape of LZR-ACC-H1 and the reason the deny-list treats CloseAccount as a value-moving instruction (WRD-DENY-01), not a housekeeping one.

title: A non-zero program_allowlist_id must name an allocated registry list
statement: A grant carrying a non-zero program_allowlist_id is rejected (InvalidAllowlistId) unless the account is bound to a Registry AND the id names an ALLOCATED list (>=1 live entry) in that Registry, loaded and checked at grant time — so no session can hold a dangling reference to an unallocated, out-of-range, or unreferenced list. Structural range validity (is_valid_list_id) is necessary but not sufficient; allocation (is_allocated_list) is the binding gate.
notes: Inverted at Task 3 (WRDF-0044): the Phase-1A 'must be 0' rule became 'must resolve to an allocated list'. The negative test inverted with it rather than being deleted, per the original note. Before Phase 1C makes the Registry mutable, specify whether existing sessions bind a list epoch/hash or require fresh regrant when a list is later expanded.

title: Grant shape limits are enforced, not assumed
statement: A grant carries at most MAX_CAPS_PER_GRANT = 2 caps, no duplicate mint, matching cap and lifetime-cap lengths, and an Ed25519 session key kind; a 2-cap grant transaction fits the 1232-byte packet.
notes: MAX_CAPS_PER_GRANT = 2 is a MEASURED byte bound (a 2-cap grant is 976 B of 1,232, and clientDataJSON may legally grow to 512 B), not a design preference. signed_slot (26a8c1e) consumed part of that headroom, so 1B must re-measure rather than assume the constant still holds.

title: Field-identity conservation on vault-owned token accounts
statement: For every account whose BEFORE snapshot is a vault-owned token account, every field except amount is byte-identical AFTER (runtime owner, token owner, mint, delegate, delegated_amount, close_authority, state, is_native, data_len, TLV-tail hash) and the after-state independently satisfies policy (state == Initialized, delegate == None, close_authority == None).
notes: Before/after, not after-only: a pre-existing delegate that the CPI CLEARS would pass an after-only check. COption tags decode strictly (0=None, 1=Some, anything else = parse error), never `tag != 0`. The 1A spike proved the comparison function by unit test only, never end to end through a real mutating CPI. B4 (2026-08-23): promoted on per-field unit coverage in conservation/tests.rs PLUS two real mutating-CPI end-to-end paths (execute + swap), which closes the note's stated hole. Caveat: in the owner/mint cases the deciding check fires one rule earlier (after-token-None / NewVaultAccountRejected), so the :219 field terms for owner_program and mint are defence-in-depth, not the asserted mechanism. The SPL-vs-T22 program tag has no isolated test and is not in the enumerated field list.

title: Outflow is coalesced per mint before a single debit
statement: outflow[mint] is summed across ALL vault-owned token accounts of that mint (negative = inflow, floored at 0 for cap purposes) and passed to exactly one buckets::debit call per mint per instruction.
notes: Per-account debiting would let N accounts of one mint each spend per_tx. The negative test is two vault ATAs of the same mint each draining just under per_tx. B4 (2026-08-23): the missing multi-account case is now covered end-to-end — two vault ATAs of one mint, 2x600_000 coalescing past a 1_000_000 per-tx cap, then 2x400_000 succeeding with a single 800_000 bucket debit.

title: The SOL equation counts each lamport exactly once
statement: outflow[SOL] = (pda_lamports_before - pda_lamports_after) + sum over vault NATIVE accounts of (account_lamports_before - account_lamports_after); a native account's value is its LAMPORTS, not its cached `amount` (which only moves on SyncNative); native lamports are counted here and are exempt from the lamports-unchanged rule; non-native CloseAccount rent enters only via the decoder's decoded close intents (spec 5.2 rule 4a).
notes: A permitted vault-sweep close returns rent as an increase in the PDA's own lamports, which the equation already sees; adding it again double-counts. The not-to-the-vault backstop (add lamports_before to outflow[SOL]) must be tested with the decoder stubbed out. WRDF-0011 (A0 round 7): native value is LAMPORTS, not the SyncNative-updated `amount` cache — the earlier amount_before-amount_after wording was the vulnerability. is_native must agree with the native mint key. Task 5 must wire the lamport-based equation and add a real-CPI SyncNative+Transfer regression.

title: Mint authority fields are byte-identical
statement: Whenever a vault-owned token account of mint M is writable, M's mint account must be present; if the vault holds any authority on M, every authority field (mint_authority, freeze_authority, and for Token-2022 transfer_fee_config_authority / withdraw_withheld_authority, extracted by TLV type and offset) is compared byte-for-byte and any change is an instruction reject, not an accounting entry.
notes: A whole-tail hash is NOT the mint control: legitimate transfer_fee accrual mutates withheld_amount in the same tail and would fail on the happy path. supply is snapshotted but is not an authority field.

title: A vault-owned token account may not disappear
statement: A vault-owned token account present BEFORE that does not exist or does not parse AFTER is a reject, unless the payload decoder handed the comparison a matching decoded close intent for that exact account; nothing downstream may infer a close from a disappearance.
notes: This is the control that catches a CloseAccount nested inside another program's CPI: the decoder cannot establish amount_before == 0 or the destination for a nested close, so it never emits an intent and the disappearance rejects here.

title: accounts_hash binds the logical list
statement: accounts_hash is computed over the LOGICAL account list in logical order (logical[0]=smart_account, logical[1]=signer, logical[2+k]=remaining_accounts[k]), hashing pubkey || is_signer || is_writable for each; no payload index ever refers to a physical slot and no code indexes the raw account slice.
notes: LZR-ACC-C1 is the nearest-miss: LazorKit bound accounts by index, not pubkey, so reordering the account list under a captured signature swapped the transfer recipient. Required negative tests: reorder accounts under a captured signature; duplicate a key in the logical list (a duplicate shifts every later index); omit an account the payload referenced. 2026-08-21 (Task 5, WRDF-0053): the duplicate-list clause is now enforced over the WHOLE logical list (named accounts included), not only remaining-vs-remaining, in the handler before hashing/auth/snapshot/dispatch (DuplicateLogicalAccount, 6059); the reorder clause is covered by the LazorKit negative. The omit-an-account clause is implicit (a payload index past the list is PayloadInvalid via resolve_payload). 2026-08-21 (Task 8, WRDF-0071): the CLIENT mirror WRD-EXEC-11 reproduces this hash from the SAME logical list, including fee-payer coalescing (the runtime promotes the fee payer to signer+writable and the handler hashes those runtime flags), so an SDK that hard-codes logical[1] read-only fails ChallengeMismatch on a self-submit.

title: No inner instruction may set a delegate on a vault-owned token account
statement: No DIRECT inner instruction of execute may set, change or clear a delegate on a vault-owned token account (the decoder deny-list refuses Approve/ApproveChecked/Revoke on both paths), and no CPI — direct or nested — may leave a DURABLE delegate change: delegate and delegated_amount must be byte-identical before vs after AND None/0 in both snapshots. A transient same-CPI set-use-clear inside a forwarding program's own execution restores field identity and is NOT observable by any before/after comparison — that case is the accepted spec §5.3 external-program boundary, bounded by the net per-mint conservation caps, and product claims must not state the absolute.
notes: Doubly enforced by design: the deny-list rejects Approve/ApproveChecked/Revoke in the decoder (WRD-DENY-01) and the field-identity comparison rejects any delegate change reached another way (WRD-EXEC-01). Both controls must be tested independently so neither passes only because the other fired first. 2026-08-21 (Task 5 round 3, WRDF-0056): statement NARROWED from the absolute 'no inner instruction may set/change/clear' to exactly what the two controls enforce — direct-payload denial (WRD-DENY-01) + durable before/after identity (WRD-EXEC-01). A forwarding CPI receiving the vault's propagated signature can Approve, use the delegate, and Revoke within its own execution; the AFTER snapshot equals the BEFORE, so field identity passes and only net value movement is charged. Closing that would require typed-adapter-only vault signing (the Task-6+ direction); until then the honest claim is the narrowed one.

title: Program owner is compared, not just field values
statement: The before/after snapshot compares each account's runtime program owner, so an account that is transferred out, closed and reopened under a program that fakes the SPL token byte layout fails the comparison.
notes: Swig's sign_v1 checked end-state field values (balance, mint, token-account owner FIELD) but never the account's actual program owner: transfer out -> close -> reopen under a fake-layout program passed every check, full drain from a 1-lamport-permission role. Snap.owner_program covers it -- the point of this entry is that it must be TESTED, not merely present. B4 (2026-08-23): a prior session recorded this as having NO covering test; that was WRONG — runtime_program_owner_change_is_rejected is exactly the SWIG-ACC-C1 reopen-under-a-fake-program case. Caveat: no test ISOLATES the owner_program term as the deciding check, because snapshot_one only decodes token fields for SPL/T22 owners, so a fake-owner account's AFTER token is None and the reject fires a line earlier. A case where ONLY owner_program differs and both sides still parse is unreachable (SPL requires exactly 165 B). No end-to-end owner-mismatch after a real CPI: the direct reincarnation route is cut earlier by the deny-list.

title: Token-2022 danger extensions reject unconditionally in 1B
statement: permanent_delegate (12), transfer_hook (14) and confidential-transfer mints (4/5) reject unconditionally; transfer_fee (1) also rejects in 1B because the allow-list machinery is 1C. The decision is made by inspecting the mint's TLV, which is why the mint account must be present.
notes: Three classes, not two: (i) deny-never-allow-listable, (ii) allow-listable in 1C with an inequality, (iii) confidential transfer = permanent non-goal, unverifiable by construction, never a policy toggle. 1B's blanket reject is a TIGHTENING of this rule, not a different one.

title: Adapter-decoded max_in and a pinned source ATA bound the call
statement: Before any inner CPI runs, the adapter parses max_in out of the inner instruction's own data (never inferred from balances) and compares it against the session per_tx and the account buckets, and the adapter's role validator requires the inner instruction's source account to be the specific vault ATA the caller declared.
notes: DESIGN BET, not a proven property (spec 5.3). A net before/after snapshot at ANY granularity cannot observe a same-CPI round trip: 100 SOL out and 99.5 SOL back inside one CPI presents a net delta of 0.5. 1B introduces no gross_turnover field and no gross bucket. The product statement must not claim conservation bounds intra-CPI turnover. 2026-08-21 (Task 5, WRDF-0051): max_in itself stays UNIMPLEMENTED (Task 6/swap), but the exposure it leaves in generic execute is closed in the interim by failing closed on the Jupiter v6 program id in the handler (JupiterViaSwapOnly, 6058) on BOTH paths, which steers the common DIRECT-route mistake toward swap. Round-2 (WRDF-0051) corrected the over-claim: a forwarding program can still reach Jupiter NESTED (reject_jupiter sees only the direct target), so this does NOT make Jupiter unreachable. The bound that holds for any nested value movement is conservation's NET per-mint cap; the intra-CPI max_in/quote-sanity bound is the accepted spec §5.3 boundary and remains swap's job (Task 6). Covered by execute::reject_jupiter_fires_on_the_v6_program_and_passes_others and tests/execute.rs::session_jupiter_via_generic_execute_rejected. 2026-08-21 (Task 6 swap round 1): swap decodes the declared in_amount from a FIXED 19-byte tail and bounds max_in ≤ caps BEFORE the CPI, but the tail is suffix-decouplable (WRDF-0059) so it is ADVISORY; the REALIZED bound is post-CPI net conservation (in_mint ≤ max_in) + a post-CPI treasury-fee-taken proof, and (root) route_hash byte-binding. A hard pre-CPI guarantee needs a byte-exact route_plan parse (WRDF-0031), owed before mainnet. Native swaps rejected in 1B (WRDF-0061).

title: SDK wrap reproduces the handler's logical list and privileges, or fails closed
statement: The client's wrapForExecute builds the COMPLETE outer execute instruction (named optionals + the real fee payer + remaining), compiles and decompiles it, and derives the accounts_hash from the resulting EFFECTIVE (runtime-coalesced) instruction metas — one source of truth, matching what the handler hashes from runtime AccountInfo. Every privilege a payload reference requests is a SUBSET of the effective outer logical meta (the PDA's invoke_signed signature excepted), enforced by a client guard. Any shape the ABI cannot honor is REJECTED, never silently rewritten: a third-party signer, a writable SmartAccount PDA, or a writable root/session signer (all fail-closed). A writable idx-0 is expressible only through the raw encodeExecutePayload codec (cross-language fixture); a typed vault-sweep CloseAccount builder is a deferred client deliverable, not implemented.
code_ref: packages/core/src/execute/wrap.ts (wrapForExecute: compile/decompile effective-metas derivation + fail-closed rejects)

evidence.name: hashes logical[1] writable when signer is the payer, read-only for a separate relayer
hashes logical[1] writable when a writable named optional aliases the signer
rejects an inner instruction that requires a third-party signer
rejects an inner instruction that names the SmartAccount PDA writable
rejects an inner instruction that names the root/session signer writable
holds the payload⊆outer privilege-subset invariant on a normal shape
reproduces the committed coalesced-logical golden and its pinned structure
generate() emits exactly the five goldens through the injected sink, no disk write
the gen-fixtures runner does not generate when imported (main-module check false)

notes: Client mirror of WRD-EXEC-06. WRDF-0071 (r1+r2): the hash is derived from the compiled instruction so fee-payer and signer-aliased-optional coalescing match the handler. WRDF-0074/0073/0079: a third-party signer, a writable PDA, or a writable signer is rejected fail-closed — the payload-subset-of-outer guard makes 'reflected or rejected' explicit. WRDF-0078: writable-PDA is narrowed to codec-expressibility; no helper is claimed to exist. WRDF-0081: ts_coalesced_logical_hash_matches is an INDEPENDENT oracle — Rust's own compute_accounts_hash confirms the SDK's coalesced hash. LZR-ACC-H2 is the signed-layout-drift prior art. WRDF-0081: the coalesced fixture is now a READ-ONLY golden vector (scripts/gen-fixtures.ts is the sole writer); the TS test asserts wrapForExecute reproduces it with an independently pinned logical list, and the gate's git-diff guard prevents any silent self-update. WRDF-0081(r5): the coalesced pin is now a literal four-entry vector (not generator-derived), and fixtures-data.ts is side-effect-free (generation only via the gen-fixtures runner under a main-check) with a re-import-no-write regression.

title: SDK wrap satisfies the execute liveness budget
statement: The client's wrapForExecute produces a transaction that meets the on-chain execute liveness budget: ComputeBudget instructions are hoisted TOP-LEVEL; the SetComputeUnitLimit is strictly decoded and validated against a measured floor and Solana's ceiling; a RequestHeapFrame is ALWAYS attached, sized from the real heap drivers (inner-instruction count, account references, payload bytes) and clamped to [128 KiB floor, 256 KiB ceiling] as a multiple of 1024, and a caller-supplied frame is preserved ONLY if it clears the runtime's alignment + range rules and covers the shape; and the on-chain account caps are enforced client-side from the effective post-coalescing privileges so an over-cap shape fails fast.

evidence.name: always attaches a RequestHeapFrame at or above the measured floor
keeps a dApp price setting AND still injects a validated compute-unit limit
rejects a dApp compute-unit limit below the measured floor
rejects a configured default limit below the floor
validates a caller-supplied heap frame against the runtime range and alignment
counts a payer-promoted remaining account against the writable cap
rejects a shape past the on-chain account cap

notes: WRDF-0072 (r1+r2): the frame is sized by inner-instruction count (255 empty ixs OOM at remainingLen==1). WRDF-0076: the CU limit is decoded and floored at ~113k handler cost (120k). WRDF-0077: caps count effective post-coalescing writability. WRDF-0080: a caller-supplied frame is validated against Agave's MIN/MAX + 1024-alignment before being kept, else rejected — a misaligned or over-ceiling frame would revert the tx on-chain.

title: `frozen` gates every 1A outflow and every grant
statement: While SmartAccount.frozen is set, no Phase 1A instruction that moves value or widens authority succeeds: `transfer` on both the session and the root path, and `grant_session`.
notes: SCOPED TO THE 1A SURFACES DELIBERATELY. `execute`, `swap` and `execute_pending` are covered by WRD-FRZ-03 at `unimplemented`; naming them here would have let 1A tests stand as evidence for instructions that do not exist. A frozen-gate negative test is on the acceptance checklist for each of them.

title: A freeze is not a brick
statement: rotate_nonce still succeeds while frozen, so the root can always prove liveness and reach unfreeze; freeze blocks value movement, not the root ceremony itself.
notes: The 1A unfreeze timelock is read LIVE from policy.timelock_secs at lift time. 1B's set_policy must make a deliberate choice for an already-frozen account: preserve the live read, or snapshot at freeze time. That decision opens a new invariant when it lands.

title: 1B value paths refuse while frozen
statement: execute, swap and execute_pending each refuse while frozen, re-validated against CURRENT state at execution rather than at queue time.
notes: execute_pending is permissionless after execute_after, so the frozen check is the only thing standing between a queued action and a freeze that landed after it was queued. B4 (2026-08-23): DELIBERATELY NOT PROMOTED. The statement is a conjunction over execute, swap and execute_pending; `execute_pending` does not exist in the program (Phase 1C), so no evidence can satisfy the row. Both built paths are enforced (execute.rs / swap.rs refuse on current state before authorization) and are now BOTH tested — execute_frozen_rejected plus the new swap_frozen_rejected, which closes a real hole (swap had no frozen test at all). To promote in 1C you additionally need an execute_pending-while-frozen test where the freeze lands AFTER queueing, which is the point of this row.

title: Proof of possession at account creation
statement: create_account cannot succeed without a valid root ceremony over the derived address, and the address itself is Keccak256("WARDEN/seed/v1" || root_pubkey33 || salt32) computed on-chain, so the PDA cannot be squatted with an attacker-controlled root: a different root derives a different address, and the victim's address cannot be reached without the victim's passkey.
notes: CLOSED by Phase 1B Task 2b. Also referred to as WRD-PoP-01 in the Phase 1B plan prose; WRD-ROOT-01 is the canonical id. RED evidence: at d0072fd an executable exploit created the victim's PDA under the attacker's root and locked the victim out (task-2b-report.md). The seed derivation is stronger than Squads' fix (require create_key to sign) because it needs no extra signer. Two Phase-1A gaps close with it: creation is now top-level-only, and an off-curve root x cannot be created because the precompile cannot verify a signature under a point it cannot decompress. Cost: MAX_MINTS_AT_CREATE fell from 4 to 1 (see WRD-BUF-05). Keep the squat-race negative test forever. Evidence sha 50dc590 is the Task 2b commit itself.

title: Root instructions are transaction-level only
statement: Every root instruction requires get_stack_height() == TRANSACTION_LEVEL_STACK_HEIGHT, so a root path can never be invoked through a middleman program.
notes: Landed in 26a8c1e. The negative test drives a real CPI caller (programs/test-middleman, test-only, never deployed) rather than stubbing the stack height, which is the only version of this test worth having. Distinct from the pre-existing self-CPI rejection, which only blocks warden->warden. Adopted from LazorKit (MIT). Held at test-covered, not higher: one caller shape is proven, not the whole space of intermediate programs.

title: User verification is mandatory
statement: authenticatorData must have both UP and UV set; a UP-only assertion is rejected.
notes: The credential is created with userVerification: required and ES256 only; the on-chain UV check is what makes that client-side request non-advisory.

title: rpIdHash is SHA-256 of the FULL origin, read from state
statement: rp_id_hash equals SHA-256("chrome-extension://<id>") -- not SHA-256("<id>") -- it is recomputed on-chain from the stored origin at creation, read from SmartAccount state on every verification, and never taken from caller-supplied instruction data or a compiled-in literal.
notes: The naive reading of the WebAuthn spec rejects EVERY assertion; measured in spike 2b. Open L9 lane, NOT covered by this invariant: the extension id changes between a dev-loaded and a store build and there is no migration path for an account created under the old one.

title: Precompile binding and ordering
statement: The root path binds exactly one secp256r1 precompile instruction, named by index in its own instruction data, at a lower index than the warden instruction, executed by the real secp256r1 program id, carrying exactly one signature whose (pubkey, message, signature) equal (root.pubkey, authenticatorData || SHA256(clientDataJSON), sig).
notes: L0 DEPENDENCY NOW SATISFIED (26a8c1e): programs/warden/tests/sigverify_wiring.rs asserts BOTH directions -- a valid signature makes the transaction succeed, and a forged one is rejected by the precompile, not by us. Only the pair proves the runtime actually runs ECDSA; either alone is compatible with a harness that verifies nothing. litesvm must stay pinned with the `precompiles` feature (LiteSVM::default() starts with every feature off) and .claude/test-gate.sh additionally asserts the feature RESOLVES -- which is a different failure mode from the runtime gate, so both are required. `fee_payer_identity_neither_authorizes_nor_blocks` is the control that stops the whole suite passing on the outer transaction signature.

title: Strict depth-0 clientDataJSON scanner
statement: clientDataJSON is rejected above MAX_CLIENT_DATA_LEN (512 B); the object is walked at depth 0 only; exactly one top-level type/challenge/origin is required and any duplicate top-level key rejects; JSON escapes are decoded before comparison or the value is rejected; type == "webauthn.get"; origin equals the stored origin; challenge equals base64url(transcript hash); a present crossOrigin must be the JSON boolean false. Byte-substring matching is forbidden.
notes: LazorKit's regression vector {"tokenBinding":{"id":"x}y"},"challenge":"real"} -- a } inside a nested string desynced their brace-depth tracker and mis-located challenge -- is ported and rejected. This is one of the two designated Trident fuzz targets (L4); the other is the 1B ExecutePayload parser.

title: cluster_tag domain separation
statement: cluster_tag is a 32-byte client-attested domain separator stored at creation, non-zero-checked, immutable in 1A, and bound into the transcript so an assertion produced against one stored tag cannot be replayed against an account holding a different tag.
notes: STATED LIMIT: it is NOT a verified genesis binding. A Solana program cannot read the cluster's genesis hash, so the value is whatever the extension wrote at create_account. It does not guarantee the tag names the cluster the transaction lands on. Codex flagged this in the 1A pilot as a finding; it was adjudicated a false positive because transcript.rs:69-76 documents the deferral -- in a file the reviewer had not been shown. That is why sibling files are now mandatory in every review prompt.

title: Generation-bump semantics (helper-driven)
statement: A transcript carrying a generation other than the account's current generation is rejected, and a session's authority is scoped to the generation it was granted under.
notes: EVIDENCE CAVEAT, STATED PLAINLY: the covering tests advance `generation` through a test helper / a revoke-and-regrant cycle, NOT through a real `execute_recovery`. They prove the CHECK, not the BUMP. The property that actually matters to a user -- that recovery invalidates every outstanding assertion, session, stage and pending action -- is WRD-ROOT-11, seeded at `unimplemented` because `execute_recovery` is Phase 1C and does not exist.

title: action_hash binds the complete semantic inputs
statement: action_hash = Keccak256(op_type:u8 || borsh(op_args)) where op_args contains every semantic input of the instruction the root authorises; the program recomputes it from the instruction it is executing and rejects on mismatch, so no argument or account can be swapped after the passkey ceremony.
notes: The op_type byte is the discriminator LZR-ACC-M2 was missing; op_bytes_are_distinct + op_bytes_are_pinned keep it from collapsing. 1B extends op_args to execute/swap (the exact compiled instruction list, or the Stage hash) and that re-opens this invariant for those ops. 2026-08-21 (Task 6 swap round 1): root swap now binds the EXACT route bytes via SwapBody.route_hash = Keccak256(route_data) (WRDF-0058), so a captured assertion cannot substitute the route_plan/quote/staged content.

title: Transcript preimage byte layout is pinned across the language boundary
statement: transcript_hash = Keccak256("WARDEN/root/v1" || cluster_tag[32] || program_id[32] || account[32] || generation:u64LE || policy_version:u32LE || root_nonce:u64LE || expiry_ts:i64LE || signed_slot:u64LE || action_hash[32]), and the Rust program, the packages/core TS mirror and the IDL agree on it byte for byte.

evidence.name: does not treat expiryTs and signedSlot as interchangeable

notes: HELD DOWN DELIBERATELY -- the layout is right, the GATE is missing. 26a8c1e added signed_slot to Rust, the packages/core mirror and the IDL together, and both sides pin vectors including a max-slot one and an adjacency test (expiry_ts and signed_slot are adjacent fixed-width integers, so a mirror that swapped them would still hash something). But the vectors are HAND-SYNCED: the TS test hard-codes hex copied from the Rust test, so a coordinated edit to both drifts silently and nothing fails. Only a generated cross-language golden-vector gate (Task 9 / L9) promotes this row. LZR-ACC-H2 is exactly this class.

title: Recovery invalidates everything outstanding
statement: A successful execute_recovery replaces the root and increments generation, and that increment invalidates every outstanding assertion, session, stage and pending action -- proven end to end through the real instruction, not a test helper.
notes: Seeded now because WRD-ROOT-08's evidence advances `generation` via a helper and a revoke/regrant cycle, which proves the CHECK but not the BUMP. Without this row the ledger would read as if recovery invalidation were already covered. Phase 1C.

title: Fixed deny-list, on both paths, above the registry
statement: SetAuthority, Approve, ApproveChecked and Revoke on SPL Token and Token-2022 are rejected in the execute payload decoder on BOTH the session and the root path, before dispatch and before any registry lookup; CloseAccount is rejected unless ALL of: it is a direct payload instruction (not nested inside another program's CPI), the account's amount_before is exactly 0, the decoded destination is the SmartAccount PDA, and the account is neither the PDA itself nor a Mint.
notes: Instruction tags (SetAuthority 6, Approve 4, Revoke 5, CloseAccount 9, ApproveChecked 13) are UNVERIFIED against SPL source. The implementer re-derives each from spl-token's TokenInstruction enum at the pinned crate version, records crate version + source path in docs/program/PHASE1B-MEASUREMENTS.md, and a unit test asserts each constant equals what the crate encodes. A wrong tag here is a silent hole, not a compile error. The decoder is a whitelist of closes it can PROVE, not a blacklist of closes it dislikes. 2026-08-21 (Task 8, WRDF-0073): parse_payload accepts a writable idx-0 structurally (the writable-PDA rule lives in enforce_pda_writable), and the TS codec now matches — so the deny-list's one CloseAccount exception (rent to the PDA) is expressible through the canonical SDK. Cross-language fixture programs/warden/tests/fixtures/payload_writable_pda_close.bin pins the parity. B4 (2026-08-23): the deny-scan unit test now parametrises over BOTH SPL Token and Token-2022 for all four tags (8 cases); previously only SPL Token was exercised, so the 'and Token-2022' half of the statement was unproven. Root-path SetAuthority added.

title: No registry entry can re-enable a denied pair
statement: A registry (or policy) list containing a denied (program, instruction) pair still fails closed: the decoder runs first, there is no override flag, and the deny-list is unreachable by the section 5.4 loosening lattice.
notes: Section 5.4 says loosening EXTENDS the registry, so a deny that lived only in the registry would not be a floor at all -- and the root path skips the registry entirely, so a deny enforced at registry_allows would not cover the root path in any form. The required negative test is a registry list containing SetAuthority that still fails closed. B4 (2026-08-23): previously ZERO coverage. The new test plants a real registry entry for (SPL_TOKEN_ID, SetAuthority) in list 1 and asserts DENY_LISTED — not RegistryDenied — which is what proves the decoder runs BEFORE the registry rather than the registry merely failing to match. A companion control test proves the planting back door is not inert (a benign planted selector IS honoured), so the main assertion cannot pass vacuously.

title: A squatted Stage is recoverable
statement: A stranger who pre-computes a victim's staged content cannot block or squat the victim's Stage: the PDA binds the creator (['stage', account, creator, hash]), so the stranger's stage and the victim's are different addresses and the victim's stage_open always succeeds — the ND-SQD3-LO-01 creator-less-seed squat is closed by construction, not merely time-boxed.
notes: Task 4. Two firms with two methods hit this exact class on Squads: Neodyme ND-SQD3-LO-01 (TransactionBuffer seeded [multisig, buffer_index], 256 slots, one Initiate-permission member fills all 256 with unclosable garbage) and Certora H-01 (transaction buffer may become inaccessible and unclosable). Seeds must bind the creator, or the count must be unbounded-but-cleanable -- pick one and test the other's failure mode.

title: No unbounded uncleanable buffer
statement: There is no per-account fixed slot table an attacker can exhaust (each (account, creator, content) is its own PDA), and every Stage — finalized or not — has a permissionless closure path after expiry_ts that returns the rent to its creator (Certora H-01 lifecycle GC).
notes: Task 4. The vault must never fund Stage rent (spec 5.2 rule 4: account creation is always funded by the outer fee payer), or the squat becomes a rent drain of the shape audited on revoke_session.

title: Every root-ceremony transaction fits the 1232-byte packet
statement: A complete root ceremony transaction (secp256r1 precompile instruction + the warden instruction) serialises to at most MAX_TX_BYTES = 1232 for freeze, unfreeze, a 2-cap grant_session, and root transfer of SOL and of an SPL token.
notes: The budget is tight: the 1A root ceremony uses 680 B, leaving ~552 B of payload headroom, and clientDataJSON may legally grow to 512 B. WRD-NONCE-03's signed_slot consumes part of that headroom -- 1B RE-MEASURES and these tests must be re-run, not assumed.

title: Every session transaction fits the 1232-byte packet
statement: A session-signed transfer of SOL and of an SPL token each serialise to at most MAX_TX_BYTES = 1232.
notes: The 40-account cap on session execute is PROVISIONAL and byte-driven, not CU-driven: a real 43-account Jupiter route serialised to 1,235 B while a 35-account route fit. That 35-43 band is a totalKeys measurement; writableKeys and executeAccountCount were never captured. 1B must re-derive it.

title: create_account packet limits are measured, not assumed
statement: A create_account transaction carrying its mandatory proof-of-possession ceremony fits the 1232-byte packet at MAX_MINTS_AT_CREATE = 1 mint (cap + ceiling + threshold) and does NOT fit at 2, and more than MAX_MINTS_AT_CREATE mints is rejected on-chain.
notes: Re-measured for Phase 1B Task 2b: proof of possession adds 477 B (182 B precompile instruction, 226 B RootArgs, the Instructions sysvar account), so 0 mints = 949 B, 1 mint = 1117 B, 2 mints = 1285 B (53 B over) and MAX_MINTS_AT_CREATE dropped 4 -> 1. Mints 2..8 are added later by Phase 1C set_policy. The negative tests are the load-bearing half: they are what stops a future constant bump from producing unlandable transactions. create_with_pop_transaction_sizes_are_measured_and_bounded asserts the constant EQUALS the largest count that actually fits, so it cannot drift from the measurement. Evidence sha 50dc590 is the Task 2b commit itself.

title: stage_finalize checks the content hash and records generation + policy_version
statement: stage_finalize requires written == len and Keccak256(data) == hash (the content-address is verified, not assumed), and records the bound SmartAccount's live generation and policy_version — the account PDA re-derived from its stored seed so a planted copy cannot supply a forged generation. The execute-time consume/current-state check is WRD-STAGE-02.
notes: Task 4. TOB-SQUADS-8 is the adjacent class: ephemeral signer seeds derived only from the batch key rather than per transaction, so all transactions in a batch shared one ephemeral keypair. Any PDA whose seeds do not uniquely bind (tx index, creator, nonce) reproduces it -- which is why Stage addressing and execute's invoke_signed seeds are both in scope here.

title: Staged content is single-use and bound to current account state at execution
statement: execute (root or session) accepts a finalized Stage only when its recorded generation and policy_version still equal the account's current values, verifies Keccak256(stage.data) == the signed payload_hash, and closes the Stage on success so it cannot be replayed; a failed execute reverts, leaving the Stage and the root nonce intact for retry.
notes: Task 5 (execute). The finalize half is WRD-STAGE-01 (test-covered at Task 4); this consume half needs execute, which does not exist yet. B4 (2026-08-23): the generation and policy_version currency bindings — the substance of 'bound to CURRENT account state' — now have execute-side tests (stale-policy_version and stale-generation both rejected with StageInvalid, session path deliberately, since policy_version is inside the root transcript and a root variant would fail earlier with ChallengeMismatch). Root-nonce-intact-on-failure is asserted on the empty-staged-payload test.

title: Unit layer: per-mint net outflow, coalesced and floored
statement: compare_and_account returns outflow per mint computed from before/after snapshots: multiple vault ATAs of one mint coalesce into a single entry, intra-vault rebalances net to zero, and inflow floors to zero rather than crediting a negative outflow.
notes: UNIT LAYER ONLY (campaign plan G7): synthetic snapshots, no CPI in the loop. End-to-end enforcement through execute is WRD-EXEC-*, unimplemented until Task 5. Added retrospectively by A0; the module landed in Task 1 (f0f38ca, fixes 2023902/d394b74).

title: Unit layer: one SOL equation across WSOL and PDA lamports
statement: Wrapped-SOL value is measured by LAMPORTS, not the cached `amount`, and is decided by `is_native` (which must agree with the native mint key or the account is rejected); wrapped-SOL and PDA lamport deltas merge into one SOL number, floored once, and a native mint key never appears in by_mint.
notes: UNIT LAYER ONLY. Non-WSOL CloseAccount rent folds into the same SOL sum (a_close_to_a_stranger_charges_the_rent_as_sol_outflow). See WRD-CONS-01 note for scope. WRDF-0008 (A0 round 3): classification was mint-key-only and would have split a Token-2022 native account's delta into by_mint[9pan…]; fixed to is_native-first with both native mint keys as belt-and-braces (compare.rs account_amount, constants::NATIVE_MINT_2022 verified against vendored spl-token-2022 7.0.0 src/native_mint.rs). RED verified: the new test fails against the pre-fix classification. WRDF-0011 (A0 round 6): native value was measured by `amount`, a SyncNative-updated cache — a SyncNative+Transfer pair drained an unsynced donation with amount unchanged. Now measured by lamports, and is_native must agree with the native mint key (mismatch rejected). RED verified.

title: Unit layer: authority or identity mutation is a reject, never an accounting entry
statement: Any change to a vault token account's owner, delegate, close authority, state, is_native, data length, TLV tail, runtime program owner, or backing-mint identity/authorities is InstructionRejected/ConservationViolated — it is never converted into an outflow number; pre-existing delegates and close authorities reject even when unchanged.
notes: UNIT LAYER ONLY. owner_program in Snap is what closes the SWIG-ACC-C1 fake-layout class at this layer; the through-CPI test is Task 5's swig_acc_c1_close_and_reopen_under_fake_layout_rejected. WRDF-0012 (A0 round 6): several unmodeled T22 mint extensions (MintCloseAuthority, InterestBearingConfig, MetadataPointer, group/member pointers, ScaledUiAmountConfig, PausableConfig) carry reassignable authorities no compared field would see, and the mint tail hash is never compared; 1B now fails closed on any required mint with an unmodeled extension. RED verified.

title: Unit layer: accounts cannot appear, vanish, or move without an explanation
statement: A vault token account that disappears without a matching CloseIntent, appears vault-owned only in the AFTER snapshot, changes list position, or duplicates another pubkey is rejected; a legal vault-sweep close is counted once and only once.
notes: UNIT LAYER ONLY. The became-vault-owned rejection (NewVaultAccountRejected, 6051) is round-1 fix C2, evidenced here directly. See WRD-CONS-01 note for scope. Prior art corrected per WRDF-0005: LZR-ACC-C1 is the position-vs-identity class; TOB-SQUADS-7 (unauthenticated creation) belongs to WRD-ROOT-01, not here.

title: Unit layer: strict, fail-closed SPL / Token-2022 layout parsing
statement: Classic SPL parses only exactly 82-byte mints and 165-byte token accounts; COption tags other than 0/1 are parse errors; T22 TLV tails are walked bounded and fail closed, danger extensions each set their bit, and transfer-fee authorities are extracted by TLV type rather than hashed with the whole tail.
notes: UNIT LAYER ONLY. spl_crate_layout_lengths_are_pinned ties the 82/165 constants to the pinned spl-token crate so a dependency bump cannot silently move the layout. See WRD-CONS-01 note for scope.

title: Unit layer: conservation arithmetic cannot wrap
statement: Outflow summation uses checked arithmetic and rejects on overflow instead of wrapping; a crafted pair of snapshots whose deltas sum past u64::MAX is an error, not a small outflow.
notes: UNIT LAYER ONLY. clippy::arithmetic_side_effects is denied crate-wide as the static half of this claim. See WRD-CONS-01 note for scope.

title: Root key non-exportable, never in extension memory
statement: Warden exposes no root-export API and root private-key material never enters extension memory; session and recovery secrets are typed and cannot be used as root authority. (A platform-synced passkey may itself be backup-eligible and movable by the OS/authenticator — that is the T7 threat, outside Warden's enforcement; Warden's boundary is that IT never exports or holds root material.)
notes: Seeded by C0 (campaign plan 2026-08-20); implemented by client C2. WRDF-0024 narrowed the claim from 'non-exportable': a backup-eligible synced passkey is movable by the platform; Warden's enforceable boundary is no Warden export API and no root material in extension memory. Commit 36c7e4bee57dba4b2b7efce498d25818bcba4fb3 creates apps/extension but only owns a typed derived unwrap key; it has no WebAuthn ceremony, root-key representation, root/session conversion, provider, or export surface. Safe absence is not a completed production invariant, and the synced-passkey T7 owner decision remains open, so status stays `unimplemented`.

title: No retained password; no equality-check auth
statement: No plaintext password is retained after derivation; no password equality check substitutes for fresh cryptographic authentication.
notes: Seeded by C0; implemented by C2/C5. Status remains PARTIAL. The core has no password equality surface: every attempt derives a KEK and succeeds only through authenticated DEK unwrap. Record orchestration overwrites caller-owned password/PRF/plaintext buffers, but cannot erase a password that ever existed as a JS string. Commit 36c7e4bee57dba4b2b7efce498d25818bcba4fb3 stores only an already-derived KEK in trusted storage.session. Commit bddb0ccbab2aa55780b132fd1528b03a297e2124 adds the first extension password consumer: it snapshots and synchronously overwrites caller bytes, derives from the exact canonical record metadata, authenticates that record and full context, schema-validates and clears plaintext before activation, and never caches the password. Commit 8653fed0b922e37a3998e96ca3f33f686daeeba7 makes record v2 own the complete context, removes normal caller context selection, and requires retained-KEK wake restore to authenticate and schema-check the exact record before readiness. Commit 125ad761b3af1879f42fa13135e5a07d57721223 moves production record seal/open to revocable asynchronous Argon2id, wipes owned password copies on every path, and proves in real Chrome that a host task preempts the RFC-profile derivation and abort rejects without activating. Wrong-password, wake-tamper, and pending-derivation tests prove no session remains active. The compound row stays `unimplemented`: no browser-reachable prompt/re-prompt exists, no production Argon2 floor or attempt-rate/backoff policy is selected, below-floor records remain accepted, PRF device behavior is unverified, the measured Chrome 151 server is not the slowest supported device, and JS/VM zeroization is best effort.

title: Absolute wall-clock unlock deadlines
statement: Idle and hard unlock deadlines are absolute wall-clock values, checked on every key use and after every service-worker wake; expiry clears all session unlock material.
notes: Seeded by C0; implemented by C2. MV3 suspension is the threat; status remains PARTIAL. Core and extension lanes cover absolute idle/hard instants, live-clock checks, one stable AbortSignal, trusted-only v2 storage, synchronous lock/expiry/record-change abort and best-effort buffer clearing, late-result suppression, and selective serialized cleanup. Commits 36c7e4bee57dba4b2b7efce498d25818bcba4fb3, c3b74eb3e93c9dde6eb29141d737e49bbc57c16f, and 0e3fc0f7b7119f41777c8dbbb98eecdef26db34a establish those layers. Commit bddb0ccbab2aa55780b132fd1528b03a297e2124 adds authenticated record-to-session activation and a real seed-use lease with nested deadline/revocation/readback checks; tests prove pending replacement, unnotified swap, disappearance, and late-output cleanup. Commit 8653fed0b922e37a3998e96ca3f33f686daeeba7 upgrades wake restore from a public bundle-id check to retained-KEK authentication, strict signer-payload decode, account/bundle comparison, live-deadline checks, and exact record readback before readiness resolves true; tamper failure revokes and removes the session. Commit 125ad761b3af1879f42fa13135e5a07d57721223 adds one pending-derivation AbortController owned by the extension lifecycle. Lock, replace, clear, competing unlock, and restore revoke it; a late derivation cannot activate. A deterministic race test proves restore clears and refuses a session serialized by a just-superseded same-owner unlock. Real Chrome proves background-priority Argon2 abort rejection, while hosts without `scheduler.postTask` may still finish an initialized KDF before output suppression and WebCrypto remains non-cancellable. The row remains `unimplemented`: no browser-reachable signer, real-key wake/signature vector, approval/hardware owners, authenticated external freshness, or durable cleanup guarantee exists. Chrome cleanup rejection can leave KEK bytes, and a callback must not perform an irreversible side effect before the final check.

title: Versioned AEAD keyring envelope with contextual AAD
statement: Encrypted keyring envelopes are versioned AEAD with random nonces and AAD binding account, full extension origin, key kind, schema version, canonical cluster identity (genesis hash), and Warden program id; malformed, unknown-version, replayed-context (incl. cross-cluster), and tampered envelopes reject.
notes: Seeded by C0; implemented by C2. AAD must not bind a release hash; genesis plus program id are required because a SmartAccount PDA is not network-qualified. Status remains PARTIAL. Core tests cover strict contextual AES-256-GCM envelopes, independent password/PRF KEK wraps of one random DEK, authenticated outer metadata, canonical bounded records, hostile version/length/cost inputs, tamper/splice/cross-context rejection, deadline races, and cleanup. Commits 7e18f275a839c2d88427a104b5814bb266fe445d, c3b74eb3e93c9dde6eb29141d737e49bbc57c16f, and 0e3fc0f7b7119f41777c8dbbb98eecdef26db34a add trusted local ownership, v2 bundle binding, and live change revocation. Commit bddb0ccbab2aa55780b132fd1528b03a297e2124 defines the AAD-bound session-signer v1 plaintext as exactly a 32-byte Ed25519 seed, composes record mutation with revocation, authenticates the exact record and supplied full context on activation/use, and suppresses output when exact readback changes. Commit 8653fed0b922e37a3998e96ca3f33f686daeeba7 makes binary record v2 self-contain canonical copy-owned AAD context, forbids caller context on v2, derives extension origin from browser runtime id, strictly tests context parser boundaries/tamper, authenticates wake restore, and leaves v1 available only for explicit core migration while the extension refuses it. Commit 125ad761b3af1879f42fa13135e5a07d57721223 exact-pins `@noble/hashes` 2.4.0, attests it in the deploy verifier, and moves production record seal/open to the asynchronous path; a real self-only-CSP Chrome extension measures RFC-profile output, host-task progress, cancellation, and password wiping. Commit cafced9c2f4725e0a95afc792fd0290acc01d28b exposes callback-lifetime copies of the already-authenticated account, genesis hash, and Warden program id and makes the still-unreachable coordinator refuse any mismatch before final key use. The row stays `unimplemented`: there is still no record-creation/onboarding or migration flow, selected production Argon2 floor, rejection/upgrade policy for below-floor records, PRF device matrix, real authoritative context resolver, browser-reachable privileged consumer, on-chain grant match, external freshness, or CAS/durability guarantee. Valid same-context replay and cleanup-retained KEK bytes remain possible.

title: Browser-owned message provenance
statement: Privileged background methods derive origin, extension id, tab, and frame from browser-owned sender metadata, never page-supplied data.
notes: Seeded by C0; implemented by client C1 (the MV3 trust boundary). Commit fcf4a255e0809a41f6b8033db12b0fb4762ff40e adds the browser-owned provider/UI sender classifiers. Commit 16663cb347707fc564698a9ac76a29ee987e9bd0 adds the strict closed provider-request parser. Commit 2975296eeff4f1096146174be41649ec399590b5 imports both provider controls into the emitted worker behind a named runtime Port: one frozen provenance tuple owns copied requests, independent 128-bit Web Crypto ids, duplicate-correlation rejection, exact-object settlement, bounded per-Port/global state, absolute expiry, and disconnect/malformed/disposal cancellation. Every valid method still returns only WARDEN_METHOD_UNAVAILABLE and the internal id is never echoed. Commit 26f3904c1d1497d81c8d3727387e62f0cc651f2a corrects the first runtime composition: Chrome requires MV3 wake listeners synchronously at top-level, so the zero-authority listener now exists before storage promises settle; a pre-ready request still returns only unavailable with zero session reads, and failed/disposed/synchronously broken bootstrap removes the listener. Commit 692e5509f7b4a62a8082aaccff2b9b89b8af315e adds the first page-reachable, default-isolated HTTP(S) bridge. It opens the exact provider Port only for a matching same-document envelope, retains browser provenance as the sole background authority, returns only the closed unavailable response, reconnects lazily after MV3 suspension, bounds one document across reconnects, and build-denies privileged dependencies in the content graph. A real unpacked-extension Chromium lane accepts top and cross-origin-frame requests, rejects a parent-frame forgery, survives same-tab navigation, forcibly removes the worker target, proves its execution global was discarded, and wakes from a later request in the same document. Commit 14205821687cf3da51abfa12866985e2a545b15a adds a single synchronous exact-name router and a separate zero-authority action-popup route without weakening the provider tuple; unknown channels close. The real Chromium lane now also rejects a popup-channel call from the actual isolated content-script world before reading its payload. The row remains unimplemented: there is no injected/registered provider, authorized account/cluster lookup, approval record/digest, success/event protocol, RPC, key use, or privileged background method. Same-page scripts remain the caller and can forge/suppress bridge traffic; unavailable-only browser vectors do not establish provenance correctness for a successful privileged path that does not yet exist.

title: Privileged UI port requires proven extension identity
statement: An extension UI port is privileged only when sender.id == chrome.runtime.id AND browser-owned sender.url/origin is the exact chrome-extension://<id> origin at an allowed extension-page path; extension-id equality alone is insufficient because an extension-owned content script shares sender.id and can call runtime.connect.
notes: Seeded by C0; implemented by C1. WRDF-0021: id-equality alone lets a content script impersonate privileged UI. Commit fcf4a255e0809a41f6b8033db12b0fb4762ff40e adds the pure classifier: same extension id plus exact chrome-extension origin, exact caller-supplied literal path allowlist, mandatory documentId, and top-frame-only handling for tab-hosted UI; the unit content-script-as-UI shape rejects. Chrome minimum is 106 because provider and tab-hosted UI identity use browser-owned MessageSender.documentId. Commits 2975296eeff4f1096146174be41649ec399590b5 and 692e5509f7b4a62a8082aaccff2b9b89b8af315e still emitted only the provider lane. Commit 14205821687cf3da51abfa12866985e2a545b15a wires the first separate UI route: the manifest action's exact /popup.html page can send only one status request and receive only WARDEN_POPUP_UNAVAILABLE; the bundle has no privileged dependency or dispatch hook. The first direct-navigation browser green was rejected because it measured a tab, not the action popup. Chromium 151 action.openPopup then measured the real browser-owned action sender as exactly id/origin/url, omitting documentId, lifecycle, tab, and frame. The corrected classifier permits that exact tabless action shape and binds it to exact extension origin/path plus Port lifetime; tab-hosted UI still requires documentId and frame 0. The same browser lane executes a forgery inside Warden's actual isolated content-script context and observes disconnect, while the action target renders and answers directly. Status stays unimplemented: the separate full-page approval route is absent, no successful privileged method consumes this distinction, Chrome 106/store/manual compatibility is unverified, and a tabless action Port has no browser-supplied document identity for per-document de-duplication.

title: Immutable single-use approval record
statement: Every approval is an immutable, expiring, single-use background record binding request id, origin, account, method, cluster, serialized message bytes and digest.
notes: Seeded by C0; V4/U7 depend on this record. Commit c3be2c1 adds the strict copy-owned record and bounded native-IndexedDB repository; f3b4946 makes the shipped worker own fail-closed startup invalidation and cleanup; d49529c adds strict canonical parsing and requested-signer binding for incoming serialized legacy/lookup-free-v0 transactions; 8c29a22 builds and reparses the exact final session-signed execute message; 349e73a signs only a claimed exact message. Commit cafced9c2f4725e0a95afc792fd0290acc01d28b adds an unshipped coordinator that creates the record only after final message construction and consumes one worker-memory authority/blockhash capsule. The row remains `unimplemented`: there is no browser route, real authoritative resolver/RPC/decoder, approval UI, navigation composition, or durable signed-result owner.

title: Approval renders exact bytes; signer rechecks digest
statement: The approval UI renders from those exact bytes and the signer rechecks the digest immediately before signing; caller labels, route params, or stale simulation objects never define the displayed intent.
notes: Seeded by C0; implemented by C3/C4. Commit c3be2c1 recomputes exact raw-message SHA-256 at repository reads/transitions; d49529c strictly owns and parses the incoming envelope; 8c29a22 builds the final message.serialize() object; 349e73a derives the sole signer from a seed, signs only those message bytes, changes only the signature slot, and reparses/verifies the result with an independent Node/OpenSSL test. Commit cafced9c2f4725e0a95afc792fd0290acc01d28b exact-compares the record/capsule, revalidates an injected authority/gate around CAS and blockhash validity, matches the keyring's account/genesis/program context, signs the claimed message, and reparses/verifies the returned bytes. The row remains `unimplemented`: no approval UI renders the bytes, the gate/resolver/RPC are fakes rather than real authorities, and no shipped route can reach the coordinator.

title: Atomic single-winner approval resolution
statement: Concurrent approve/reject/timeout/navigation events have one atomic winner and cannot sign twice or resolve the wrong request.
notes: Seeded by C0. Commit c3be2c1 real-browser tests independent IndexedDB connections, concurrent approve/reject and approve/approve, exact expiry, distinct ids with identical bytes, tamper deletion, and worker-restart cancellation; f3b4946 composes cancellation with the shipped worker readiness and stop/wake lifecycle. Commit cafced9c2f4725e0a95afc792fd0290acc01d28b consumes each in-memory capsule once, tests double approve and approve/cancel ordering, and relies on the real owner's digest CAS interface. The full row remains `unimplemented`: no browser route composes navigation/Port teardown, timeout, account/network switching, durable result replay, or nonce/send ownership with a live signature path; post-claim failure leaves an approved tombstone without a result.

notes: Seeded by C0; implemented by client C4. Commits d49529c and 8c29a22 strictly parse and structurally wrap the final execute message. title: Strict-DER parsing and mandatory low-S normalization
statement: Every browser WebAuthn assertion is parsed with strict DER (trailing bytes, non-minimal lengths, r/s out of range rejected), converted to fixed 64-byte compact form, and unconditionally low-S normalized before submission; a recorded real high-S Chrome assertion passes the on-chain precompile end to end only after normalization.
notes: Seeded by C0 (campaign plan G3/C2a). Spec:60/:232 make low-S normalization mandatory; the precompile rejects high-S and Chrome emitted high-S on the first real sample. Blocks C3/V4. C3 signing and V4's create ceremony consume ONLY assertionToCompact() output. 2026-08-22 IMPLEMENTED (C2a) @b1d5968: dependency-free assertionToCompact() in packages/core — strict DER Ecdsa-Sig-Value parse (rejects trailing bytes, indefinite/non-minimal lengths, negative/non-minimal/oversized INTEGERs, r/s out of [1,n-1]) → fixed 64-byte compact with UNCONDITIONAL low-S (s>n/2 ⇒ n−s); typed AssertionFormatError never a panic. Proven end-to-end on the RECORDED real high-S Chrome assertion (spike 02-webauthn data): normalizes to the expected low-S bytes AND the precompile-equivalent lowS verifier (@noble/curves, dev-only) REJECTS the raw high-S but ACCEPTS the normalized form. + malformed-DER red set, low-S/idempotence property (500 random), 3000-case fuzz. Blocks C3 + vanity V4 (both consume only this output). The LiteSVM precompile-acceptance cross-check remains as the C2a Rust-side end-to-end (owner/next). 2026-08-22 (C2a round-1, WRDF-0103): the strict-DER + mandatory low-S CONVERSION is implemented and unit-tested @b1d5968 (packages/core/src/webauthn/assertion.ts + test/assertion.test.ts: golden real high-S Chrome vector normalizes; a precompile-EQUIVALENT lowS verifier (@noble/curves, in-process) rejects raw-high-S and accepts the normalized form; malformed-DER red set; low-S/idempotence property; 3000-case fuzz). But WRD-SIG-01 is COMPOUND — its statement requires the recorded assertion to pass the REAL on-chain secp256r1 precompile END TO END only after normalization. The in-process Noble check is a proxy, NOT the real precompile, and assertionToCompact is not yet wired through a production ceremony builder (that is C3). So this row stays UNIMPLEMENTED: promoting it to test-covered on the conversion + a proxy verifier overclaims. Remaining acceptance: a merged-SHA test carrying the recorded assertion through assertionToCompact → a production secp256r1-precompile transaction builder → LiteSVM with_mainnet_features(), raw-high-S REJECT + normalized ACCEPT — lands alongside/after C3. The conversion code stays; it is a verified building block, not the closed invariant.

title: Structured events on every value/policy transition
statement: execute/swap/transfer emit a structured event on every successful bucket debit and every cap rejection, and freeze/unfreeze emit freeze events; the notifier counts BucketDebited and freeze-transition events only from a finalized transaction with meta.err == null (a rolled-back debit's surviving log is not a spend), and treats CapRejected/DeniedInstructionRejected as failed-transaction signals. Each event has a replay-safe identity (transaction signature + outer/inner instruction index + event ordinal) so a reconnect/backfill/restart cannot double-count a legitimate repeated debit.

Trail of Bits rated Squads logging insufficient for off-chain attack detection. WRDF-0022 round 6: payload dedup is unsafe (two identical debits are legitimate); identity is by signature+instruction+ordinal. WRDF-0022 round 7: Task 5E must also prove the event set is COMPLETE (every debit/rejection/freeze path emits) and source-authenticated (events come from the warden program id, not a look-alike); finalized at Task 5 implementation. 2026-08-21 (Task 5, WRDF-0052): confirmed still UNIMPLEMENTED and DEFERRED to Task 5E (structured events are additive to the execute authorization/conservation paths, not a fix to them); recorded with an explicit scope verdict in REVIEW-SCORECARD.jsonl rather than silence. 2026-08-21 (Task 6 swap round 1): swap likewise emits no events — same Task-5E deferral (WRDF-0052).
